method: Compared the cumulative notation entries and the ink descriptions in the decided records, using main-adjudicated crops already viewed where a reading had differed. No decided locus was recropped. This is an interim cross-page consistency review; extend through all 25 pages before freezing.

groups.finding: Upper and lower transverse strokes are represented consistently as overline plus underline. Typed unruled references on 070 are left unruled. Previously inspected crops settle the graphical distinctions; no new reading change. The separately penned VI and II in the pencil note on 075 retain both rules; the typed XI in the 074 letter has neither rule. These different physical constructions remain distinct. Scan 077 uses the same upper-and-lower-rule convention for its independently read VI, XXI, XXII and marginal XXIII. The crowded first VI/VII remains uncertain; the clear later VI does not settle it. The main reader viewed the retained first-numeral crop and separate crops of the clear groups.
Both leaves use the two-capital AR subscript. Their notation agrees; the signed continuation provides the separately documented letter attribution, not a reason to normalize other hands.

Raised points in K and Gr are bullet, and 070 explicitly contrasts raised and lowered K points. Vertical placement differs where the ink differs; no prime or star is substituted. The two Gr expressions in 071 retain raised solid points, as confirmed by all three half readings.

The hand-drawn doubled letters, the defined double A, and the separately underlined typed Q/Z are distinct observed constructions. They must not be collapsed merely because they name coefficient objects. The central Z doubt in 052 remains.

Ordinary pairs use two backticks and two apostrophes. The crowded typed opening strokes in 069 and the punctuation under the closing pair in 070 retain their independently inspected alternatives; none is normalized from another page. The 071 quoted correction pairs and the 072 quotations/ellipses retain the same convention; no new disagreement of quotation identity arose.

Graphic descriptions retain the separately observed shapes and relative positions. A superseded colon-form notation entry for 055 was removed; final page text was already graphical. The 069 notation wrappers were aligned with final inline graphics without changing their shapes or readings. Main-viewed 071 and 072 crops establish different shapes: a high oblique pair and faint over-letter traces on 071, and two irregular lobes plus a small satellite on 072. They are drawn separately, with origin and meaning uncertain, rather than normalized to a colon. The 074 hook is a single unassigned curve. The 075 pair has two visible faint companions preserved with its irregular lobes; the 076 pair has its own irregular contours, without treating the surrounding pale processing halo as additional authored punctuation. Main inspected each retained local crop; no cross-page colon normalization is made. On 085, the detached low dash belongs to a local two-component marginal configuration with a long upper hook. The main-viewed crop does not fix its textual function; its shape and relative placement are drawn rather than normalized to a question mark or colon. The 086 lowered oval beside the normal period and the raised diagonal pair above a leader line are individually reproduced from the main-viewed crops. Their smaller solid forms remain distinct from the hollow typewriter leader points. The pale channel cutting a leader point is a surface disruption and is excluded after crop comparison.

The raised letter in the handwritten 052 abbreviation and the baseline typed pt in 072 are distinct physical forms. All three 072 readings confirm both pt letters on the baseline; no superscript is transferred from the earlier hand.

The signed two-leaf letter consistently distinguishes script N and script initials in Hom/Ext from ordinary cohomology H and formula K. The introductory K on 075 alone has a doubtful doubled left stem and remains K/blackboard K; plain later copies do not erase that local ink ambiguity.

Both leaves place alg/an above the cohomological degree. Parentheses are present around alg in the first display of 076 and are preserved there; they are not supplied to the unparenthesized qualifiers in 075. The upper-right H^0 in the 075 diagram remains without alg because the three half readings agree on its absence.

The 052 eta/y uncertainty and the 076 eta/n transition glyph belong to different local contexts and pen constructions. Each is marked at its first repeated occurrence under the same convention, with its own supported alternatives. The 076 two-stem crop excludes gamma; that decision does not alter the different 052 locus.

The letter keeps superscript cohomological degrees, subscript d_2 and X_0, upper primes on local extensions, and tall restriction bars distinct. The 075 comparison has its observed vertical and horizontal arrows; the 076 local-isomorphism arrow has a single wave above. The 076 target index remains ambiguous despite the conditional composition check.

Curved grouping strokes and enclosing loops are drawn from their local paths. The upper brace of 077 has two lower return contours, whereas its lower brace has one. Neither that retracing nor the enclosing SGA 7 loop is converted to a textual deletion. All 077 shapes were personally inspected in the retained crops.

The circular character in an EGA reference on 054 and the chapter oval on 085 each retain O/0 alternatives where their local outline does not distinguish letter from digit. Chapter-number expectation does not determine the 085 glyph. These are separate local uncertainties, preserved under the same notation convention.

Recoverable underlying letters use deleted immediately before the replacement; unresolved identities remain unsure inside that state. The 085 r/p pair follows this convention. Its terminal pale s is separately uncertain in typing state: single repeated impression, corrected underprint, or closely overlapping live letters. The graphic presence is preserved without assuming a correction operation from a familiar word. On 086, the same deletion-before-replacement convention preserves six overtyped positions. The crowded i position retains l/t/j, with a low residual contour whose connection to an older j is possible but unestablished. The contour is documented as part of that same correction cluster.

groups.group: Contents headings, number fields and leaders
groups.finding: Ordinary section signs and decimal number fields remain typed text, with observed spacing and punctuation. Leaders are present or absent entry by entry: the replacement 2.4 on 085 and entries 3.10 and 6.8 on 086 do not receive supplied leaders. Both page fields retain their observed flanking dashes. Their manuscript page numbers are kept in supplied scan order.

remaining_scope: Scan 087 is being read; scans 088–098 follow in the prescribed page list. Extend this review through all 25 pages before freezing.
